context: The queue is on the left and the vertical singly linked list is on the right. The label between them reads “Linked list implementation / Queue interface.” Both run from front to rear down the page. The list’s next arrows point down, with the head at the front of the queue and the tail at the rear.
description: Nodes can be added only at the tail of the list and removed only from the head. In the initial view, the arrow beside the front points up and out of the queue. The arrow beside the rear points up into the queue from below.

frames.announcement: The initial queue has four elements, [1, 3, 2, 5]. Head node 1 is at the front and tail node 5 is at the rear.
frames.explanation: The initial list is 1 → 3 → 2 → 5, corresponding to the four-element queue [1, 3, 2, 5]. Node 1 is both the head and the front. Node 5 is both the tail and the rear.
frames.key_state: The initial queue is [1, 3, 2, 5] from front to rear. The list runs 1 → 3 → 2 → 5 from head to tail. Head node 1 is the front and tail node 5 is the rear.
frames.title: Initial queue: out at the head, in at the tail

frames.announcement: The call push(4) adds node 4 at the end of the list. Node 4 becomes the tail of the list and the rear of the queue.
frames.explanation: The call push(4) is labeled “Add node 4 to the end of the list” on the right. The old tail, 5, now points to the new teal node, 4, directly below it. The tail marker moves down to 4. The list now runs 1 → 3 → 2 → 5 → 4, the same order as the five elements in the queue from front to rear. The head and front are still 1. The tail and rear are now 4.
frames.key_state: After push(4), the queue is [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] and the list is 1 → 3 → 2 → 5 → 4. The front is still 1, and the new tail node, 4, is the rear.
frames.title: Enqueue 4 at the tail

frames.announcement: The call pop() removes head node 1. Node 3 becomes the head and front, leaving the queue [3, 2, 5, 4].
frames.explanation: The call pop() is labeled “Remove the head node” on the right. It removes and returns 1. The head marker moves down to its successor, 3. The list now runs 3 → 2 → 5 → 4, the same order as the four elements in the queue from front to rear. The head and front are now 3. The teal node, 4, is still the tail and rear.
frames.key_state: After pop() removes head node 1, the queue is [3, 2, 5, 4] and the list is 3 → 2 → 5 → 4. Head node 3 is the new front, and 4 is still the tail.
frames.title: Dequeue 1 from the head

result: With references to both the head and the tail, enqueueing at the tail and dequeueing from the head change only local references. Both take O(1) time.
summary: The head of a singly linked list serves as the front of the queue, and the tail serves as the rear. Elements enter at the tail and leave from the head.
title: Enqueueing and dequeueing with a linked list
